| Unlimited | $97/mo | $80.90/mo | Unlimited contacts, funnels, courses, automation rules |

Starting prices verified October 2026 against systeme.io's published pricing page and multiple 2026 pricing breakdowns. Always confirm your tier on the vendor's pricing page before buying.

The pricing structure tells you the business model: systeme.io wins by being cheap enough that upgrading is a non-decision. At $17/month, Startup costs less than most email tools' entry tiers — while including funnels, courses, and checkout that those tools don't have at any price.

## The free plan's real limits

The free plan is genuinely free — no credit card, no trial countdown. For a new creator it's a complete starter business: capture leads, run a funnel, host a course, send unlimited emails. But two limits matter:

1 automation rule. You get one workflow. A welcome sequence or an abandoned-cart flow or a post-purchase upsell — pick one. The moment you want real automation, you're on Startup. This is the deliberate pressure point of the whole pricing ladder, and it's fair: one rule is enough to learn the platform, not enough to run it.

3 funnels, 1 course. Fine for launching your first product. The second product forces an upgrade. Again, fair — by the time you have two products, $17/month is a rounding error.

The honest read: the free plan is a real product, not a demo. It converts because the upgrade path is obvious, not because the free tier is crippled.

## What it actually does

Systeme.io bundles six tools that are normally separate subscriptions:

Sales funnels. Drag-and-drop funnel builder with templates for lead capture, sales pages, and checkout flows. Functional and fast to launch; reviewers consistently note it's less flexible than dedicated builders (no pixel-perfect control, template designs are plain). It converts fine — it just won't win design awards.

Email marketing. Unlimited emails on every plan, campaigns plus automation rules, basic segmentation and tagging. The builder and automation logic are simpler than Kit or ActiveCampaign — good enough for product sellers, thin for email-first businesses. (More on this below.)

Online courses. Course hosting with modules, lessons, drip scheduling, and student management — included even on the free plan. Reviewers rate it as genuinely competitive with entry-level course platforms; it won't replace a dedicated LMS for complex curricula, but for selling a $49–$499 course it's complete.

Checkout and payments. Order bumps, upsells, downsells, coupons, and payment-plan options built into the funnel flow — the revenue-maximizing mechanics that usually require plugins or higher tiers elsewhere. Stripe and PayPal integrations are standard.

Webinars. Evergreen (automated) webinars on the Webinar plan and up. Live webinar functionality is the notable gap reviewers mention — if live webinars are core to your sales process, check the current feature set carefully.

Affiliate program management. Run your own affiliate program for your products, plus a marketplace where other systeme.io affiliates can promote your offers. For digital-product sellers, this is a distribution channel, not just a feature.

## Email: the weakest link

If there's one area where "adequate everywhere" dips toward "thin," it's email. The honest comparison: Kit's automation builder is in a different league — visual workflows, better segmentation, and a deliverability reputation built over a decade serving creators. Systeme.io's email gets the job done for transactional and broadcast sends around a product business, but newsletter-first creators consistently report hitting its ceilings.

The deliverability question deserves a straight answer: systeme.io is a younger, broader platform, and its shared sending reputation doesn't match dedicated email providers. For a course seller emailing buyers, this rarely matters. For a 50,000-subscriber newsletter where email is the revenue, it matters a lot. Match the tool to where your money comes from.

## Who should buy Systeme.io?

Buy it if: you're a solopreneur or small team selling courses, coaching, memberships, or digital products; you're starting from zero and want one bill; you're currently paying $100+/month across 3–4 tools and most of that spend is on features systeme.io includes; or you want to run your own affiliate program without extra software.

Don't buy it if: email is your primary channel (see Kit ); you're an agency needing client sub-accounts and white-labeling (see GoHighLevel ); you need advanced design control, deep analytics, or live webinar tooling as core requirements.

The upgrade path is the product. Start free, upgrade to Startup ($17) when you need automation, to Webinar ($47) when you need evergreen webinars, to Unlimited ($97) when volume justifies it. At no point does the math get scary — which is precisely why the platform keeps growing.

## How it compares to alternatives

We maintain full head-to-head breakdowns against systeme.io's two closest rivals:

vs Kit: Systeme.io vs Kit — email quality vs stack value for creators. Kit wins email; systeme.io wins everything-else-per-dollar.

vs GoHighLevel: GoHighLevel vs Systeme.io — the $97 question. GoHighLevel is the agency platform; systeme.io is the solopreneur platform. Different buyers, different winners.

In the all-in-one landscape: see our best all-in-one marketing platforms roundup for how systeme.io stacks against Kartra, Kajabi, and the rest on price-per-capability.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is systeme.io really free?**

Yes — the free plan is real, with no credit card required: 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels, 1 online course, 1 automation rule, and unlimited emails. The catch is the single automation rule, which limits how much selling you can automate before upgrading to Startup at $17/month.

**How much does systeme.io cost in 2026?**

Four tiers: Free ($0), Startup at $17/month, Webinar at $47/month, and Unlimited at $97/month. Annual billing discounts each paid tier to roughly $14.17, $39.17, and $80.90/month respectively. Pricing verified October 2026; the ceiling matters most — $97/month max for unlimited everything.

**Is systeme.io better than GoHighLevel?**

They serve different buyers. Systeme.io is simpler and far cheaper ($0–$97/mo) — ideal for solopreneurs selling courses or digital products. GoHighLevel ($97–$497/mo) is built for agencies with client pipelines, CRM depth, and white-labeling. Our full comparison breaks down which fits which business.

**Does systeme.io have an affiliate program?**

Yes — 60% recurring commission on every referral's subscription, for the lifetime of the customer. It's one of the most generous SaaS affiliate programs we've tracked, which is itself a signal the product's unit economics work at its price points. Lifetime recurring terms like that are rare outside early-stage tools.

**What's the catch with systeme.io?**

Three honest ones: a simpler email builder with a weaker deliverability reputation than dedicated email platforms; a functional but less flexible page/funnel builder; and ceilings on design customization and reporting depth for advanced users. It's a breadth play, not a depth play — and at these prices, that's a fair trade for most solopreneurs.

**Is systeme.io good for email marketing?**

Adequate everywhere, excellent on price — but if email is your primary revenue channel, Kit's automation justifies its price. Upgrade path is clear: Startup ($17) when you need automation, Webinar ($47) for evergreen webinars, Unlimited ($97) when volume justifies it. Buy systeme.io for the bundle; buy a specialist when email alone pays the bills.

**What's the catch with systeme.io's pricing?**

There isn't a pricing trap — that's the point. Free for 2,000 contacts, $17–$97/month tiers, $97/mo ceiling. The trade-offs sit elsewhere: rules-based automation depth (1 / 10 / 100 / unlimited rules by tier) versus visual workflow builders, and less design customization than pricier platforms.

**Can agencies use systeme.io?**

It's built for digital-product businesses, not agencies: skip it if you need white-label pipelines (that's GoHighLevel) or deep design customization. For solo operators selling courses or digital products, it's the price-to-value leader — free to start, $97/mo maximum. Agencies needing client-facing white-label should look elsewhere from the start.

## Final verdict

Worth it — and the easiest recommendation on this site. Systeme.io does what it promises: it replaces a $100–$300/month stack of single-purpose tools with one platform that starts free and caps at $97/month. The catches are real but disclosed and proportionate: simpler email, simpler pages, simpler analytics. For digital-product sellers, the value math isn't close — competitors charge systeme.io's top-tier price as their entry tier.

The one thing to get right: match the tool to your revenue. If you sell things, systeme.io's breadth is exactly what you need. If your list is your business, pay for the email specialist instead. Everything else is details — and at $0 to start, the cost of finding out is zero.

### Selling courses or digital products?

Start free — no credit card. Build your first funnel and send your first emails today; upgrade to $17/month only when automation becomes the bottleneck.

# Systeme.io vs ClickFunnels: Funnel Builders Compared for 2026

Last updated October 2026 · 11 min read · Pricing verified October 2026

In short: Pick systeme.io if you're pre-revenue or selling your first products — start free with 2,000 contacts and 3 funnels, then $17–$47/month as you grow on one bill. Pick ClickFunnels if funnels are the business: the deepest builder, biggest template library, affiliate management, training — $97–$297/month. $97 buys ClickFunnels' entry plan or systeme.io's unlimited plan.

ClickFunnels defined the category — the word "funnel" is practically branded by it. In 2024 it repriced into two plans (Startup $97/month, Pro $297/month, both with 14-day free trials and no free tier), and it remains the deepest, most polished funnel builder you can buy. Systeme.io is the budget all-in-one: funnels, email, courses, checkout, and affiliate management starting free and topping out at $97/month — exactly what ClickFunnels' cheapest plan costs.

The honest frame: ClickFunnels is the best funnel builder money can buy; systeme.io is the best business stack for money you don't want to spend. The gap between them is smaller than either company's marketing suggests, and it collapses entirely for pre-revenue businesses. Here's the full breakdown.

## Quick questions, quick answers

The questions people ask most about this comparison, answered directly. Stats and pricing verified October 2026.

**Is systeme.io really enough to replace ClickFunnels?**

If you're pre-revenue or selling your first products: yes — start free with 2,000 contacts and 3 funnels, then $17–$47/month as you grow on one bill. If funnels are the business — deep canvas testing, Backpack affiliate management on Pro, the training ecosystem — ClickFunnels at $97–$297/month earns its price.

**What's the real yearly cost difference between systeme.io and ClickFunnels?**

$97/month is the pivot: it buys ClickFunnels' entry plan or systeme.io's unlimited-everything plan — about $1,164/year for opposite things. Pre-revenue sellers and first-time sellers land on systeme.io; funnels-as-the-business buyers land on ClickFunnels.

**Can I run a funnel on systeme.io for free?**

Yes — systeme.io's free-forever plan includes 2,000 contacts and 3 funnels with no credit card required, so you can run a real funnel before paying anything. ClickFunnels offers only a 14-day trial and no free tier. That's the clearest single difference between the two platforms.

**When should I upgrade from systeme.io to ClickFunnels?**

When you hit walls systeme.io doesn't have: conditional-path funnel testing depth, Backpack affiliate management (Pro tier), or you want the ClickFunnels training ecosystem. Most pre-revenue sellers never hit that wall — start free and switch only when a specific gap appears.

## The quick verdict

Pick systeme.io if you're pre-revenue or selling your first products — start free (2,000 contacts, 3 funnels, no card), pay $17–$47/month as you grow, and run funnels, email, courses, and checkout on one bill.

Pick ClickFunnels if funnels are the business — you want the deepest builder, the biggest template library, Backpack affiliate management, and FunnelFlix training, and $97–$297/month is a real budget line, not a gamble.

The one-sentence version: $97/month buys you ClickFunnels' entry plan or systeme.io's unlimited-everything plan — choose based on whether you need a funnel machine or a whole business stack.

## What a year actually costs

Year one, pre-revenue: systeme.io Free costs $0; ClickFunnels Startup costs $1,164 from month one. With 5,000 contacts, a course, and email drips, systeme.io Startup runs $204/year versus ClickFunnels Startup at $1,164/year — roughly $960 apart. One month of ClickFunnels' entry plan costs the same as systeme.io's unlimited-everything plan.

Run three realistic scenarios — a solopreneur validating an offer, a growing creator, and an established seller:

- Year one, pre-revenue: systeme.io Free = $0. ClickFunnels Startup on the trial, then $1,164/year from month 1 — before a single sale. That's the whole comparison for most people reading this article.

- Growing list (5,000 contacts, a course, email drips): systeme.io Startup = $204/year. ClickFunnels Startup = $1,164/year, plus any email-send overage. Same funnel shape, ~$960 apart.

- Established ($97/month is real money to you): systeme.io Unlimited = $1,164/year, unlimited everything, free migration help. ClickFunnels Startup = $1,164/year — the prices converge, and now the decision is genuinely about product: ClickFunnels' builder depth vs systeme.io's inclusion of webinars, blogging, and communities.

The pattern: systeme.io wins every price comparison until your budget genuinely has $97–$297/month in it, at which point you should stop comparing prices and compare builders.

The decider: funnels as the business? ClickFunnels. Starting free or pre-revenue on one bill? systeme.io.

## The builder experience

ClickFunnels 2.0's canvas is the real product: you map entire customer journeys with conditional branches and split paths, and the editor's depth shows in the details — global styles, modular blocks, funnel stats baked into every step. Beginners routinely get lost in it; the learning curve is a documented, repeated complaint. That complexity is the price of the power.

Systeme.io's editor is deliberately minimal: pick a goal (build an audience, sell a product), and the platform lays out the squeeze page, thank-you page, and order form. Connecting a form to an automated email sequence takes a couple of clicks. It does exactly this and no more — and for one-operator businesses, "no more" is a feature. Reviews consistently praise the speed from signup to first working funnel.

The honest translation: ClickFunnels is a Formula 1 car with a steep learning curve; systeme.io is a reliable sedan with the keys already in it. Match the tool to your stage.

## Who should pick Systeme.io, and who should pick ClickFunnels?

Pick systeme.io if you're pre-revenue or selling your first products — start free with 2,000 contacts and 3 funnels, paying $17–$47/month as you grow. Pick ClickFunnels if funnels are the business: the deepest builder, biggest template library, affiliate management — at $97–$297/month.

Pick systeme.io if: you're pre-revenue or under ~$5k/month and want one bill for funnels, email, courses, and checkout; if you value starting free with no card over template depth; if webinars, blogging, or communities are part of your plan (ClickFunnels has no native webinar tool).

Pick ClickFunnels if: funnels are the business — you're running paid traffic to offers and split-testing is revenue; if you need Backpack affiliate management or 10 workspaces; if you want the template marketplace and FunnelFlix training ecosystem that a decade of category dominance built.

Skip ClickFunnels if you're validating — $97/month before revenue is how tools become regrets. Skip systeme.io if you already run a six-figure funnel operation on ClickFunnels and depend on its automation depth — the migration cost of rebuilding automations isn't worth the savings at that stage.

Pick ClickFunnels for depth; pick systeme.io when funnels are one part of an unvalidated business.

**Should I switch from ClickFunnels to systeme.io?**

Switch if your funnel is one piece of a small operation and the ClickFunnels bill funds features you don't use. Systeme.io — unlimited email sending on every plan, including free; the whole value case is that email, funnels, and courses are one bill. ClickFunnels includes email marketing too, but heavy senders hit usage add-ons ($0.675 per 1,000 sends). For newsletter-style volume on a budget, systeme.io wins; for behavioral automation depth, neither is a specialist.

Yes — systeme.io supports order bumps, one-click upsells, and downsells in its funnel checkout, plus coupons and 0% transaction fees on every plan. The gap versus ClickFunnels is polish and scale, not features: a decade of the entire company optimizing one checkout flow. For a first or second product, most sellers can't tell the difference.

**Is systeme.io really enough to replace ClickFunnels?**

If you're pre-revenue or selling your first products: yes — start free with 2,000 contacts and 3 funnels, then $17–$47/month as you grow on one bill. **What's the real yearly cost difference between systeme.io and ClickFunnels?**

Pre-revenue sellers and first-time sellers land on systeme.io; funnels-as-the-business buyers land on ClickFunnels. The same annual budget buys opposite things: entry-level depth, or unlimited breadth across everything.

**Can I run a funnel on systeme.io for free?**

**When should I upgrade from systeme.io to ClickFunnels?**

When you hit walls systeme.io doesn't have: conditional-path funnel testing depth, Backpack affiliate management (Pro tier), or you want the ClickFunnels training ecosystem. Most pre-revenue sellers never hit that wall — start free and switch only when a specific gap appears.

**Is systeme.io or ClickFunnels better for beginners?**

For beginners, systeme.io. Its editor is deliberately minimal — pick a goal and the platform lays out the pages and automated sequence in a couple of clicks. ClickFunnels' canvas is powerful but beginners routinely get lost in it; the learning curve is a documented, repeated complaint. Start free on systeme.io (2,000 contacts, 3 funnels, no card).

**Does ClickFunnels have webinars?**

No native webinar tool. If webinars are part of your plan, systeme.io's $47/month Webinar plan covers evergreen webinars — an explicit reason to pick systeme.io. On ClickFunnels you'd pay $97–$297/month for funnels with webinars still requiring a separate tool. For webinar-led selling, the gap in favor of systeme.io is decisive.

ClickFunnels, by a wide margin. Its template library is the biggest in the category, with a best-in-class canvas and global styles — the moat you're paying $97–$297/month for. systeme.io's editor is deliberately minimal: pick a goal, get the pages laid out, no marketplace. If pre-built design polish is the priority, ClickFunnels wins.

## Final verdict

Worth it for validators: systeme.io. Start free, pay $17–$47/month as you grow, and run the entire business — funnels, email, courses, checkout, affiliates — on one cheap bill. For anything pre-revenue, this comparison isn't close.

Worth it for funnel operators: ClickFunnels. Once $97–$297/month is a line item your funnel revenue justifies, the builder depth, template library, and Backpack ecosystem are genuinely worth paying for. The cheapest ClickFunnels plan costs what systeme.io's best plan costs — so at that budget, buy the specialist.

The move most people should make: start on systeme.io free, outgrow it honestly, and only switch to ClickFunnels when your funnel volume makes its depth pay. The funnel wars have one consistent loser: whoever pays $97/month before their first sale.

# Systeme.io vs Kit: Email + Funnels for Creators (2026)

Last updated October 2026 · 10 min read · Pricing verified September 2026

In short: Pick systeme.io if you sell courses, coaching, or digital products and want funnels, email, checkout, and hosting in one dashboard — starting free and capping at $17–$47/month. Pick Kit if email is your primary channel: the best automation builder in the creator space, with a free plan covering 10,000 subscribers. Sellers buy systeme.io; publishers buy Kit.

Kit (formerly ConvertKit — renamed in 2024, same product) is the email platform built for creators: visual automations, best-in-class deliverability, and a free plan that covers up to 10,000 subscribers. Systeme.io is the all-in-one challenger: email plus funnels, courses, and checkout, starting free and topping out at $97/month for unlimited everything. If you're a creator who sells things, this comparison is genuinely hard — because Kit's paid plans cost more than systeme.io's entire top tier.

The honest frame: Kit is email done properly; systeme.io is the whole business stack, cheaply. One of those is worth more than the other depending on where your revenue actually comes from. Here's the full breakdown.

## Quick questions, quick answers

The questions people ask most about this comparison, answered directly. Stats and pricing verified October 2026.

**systeme.io vs Kit — which is better?**

Different buyers. Pick systeme.io if you sell courses, coaching, or digital products and want funnels, email, checkout, and course hosting in one dashboard — starting free, paid tiers at $17–$97/mo. Pick Kit if email is your primary channel: the best automation builder in the creator space, with a free plan covering 10,000 subscribers.

**How much does Kit cost for 10,000 subscribers?**

Kit's Creator plan is priced per subscriber: $39/mo ($33/mo annual) for 1,000, ~$139/mo at 10,000, ~$379/mo at 50,000. Kit's free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers, but sequences and unlimited automations need a paid plan. That pricing curve is the main argument for systeme.io's flat $97/mo Unlimited.

**Is systeme.io actually free?**

Yes, for real: the $0 plan includes 2,000 contacts, 3 funnels, 1 course, 1 automation rule, and unlimited emails with no credit card. Paid tiers: Startup $17/mo ($14.17/mo annual), Webinar $47/mo ($39.17/mo annual), and Unlimited $97/mo for unlimited everything.

**Which is better for selling courses: systeme.io or Kit?**

This one isn't close. systeme.io wins for course sellers: course and membership hosting is built in on every plan, including free, alongside funnels and checkout. Kit is email-first — basic landing pages and forms only, with commerce features limited to digital products. If courses are the product, systeme.io is the tool.

**What's the real catch of systeme.io's $97/mo Unlimited plan?**

Automation depth and deliverability. systeme.io's automation is rules-based (1 / 10 / 100 / unlimited rules by tier) versus Kit's visual workflows with subscriber scoring and A/B testing — and its deliverability is solid but not the best-in-class reputation Kit holds with creators. Unlimited everything at $97/mo is real; it just trades depth for breadth.

## The quick verdict

Pick systeme.io if you sell courses, coaching, or digital products and want funnels, email, checkout, and course hosting in one dashboard. Starting free and capping at $17–$47/month, it's the cheapest credible all-in-one in the market.

Pick Kit if email is your primary channel — newsletter-first creators, writers, podcasters — and you want the best automation builder and deliverability in the creator space, with a free plan that covers 10,000 subscribers.

The one-sentence version: systeme.io wins on stack value for sellers; Kit wins on email quality for publishers. Kit's free plan is so generous many creators never pay either tool.

## Pricing compared, tier by tier

The pricing models are mirror images: systeme.io prices by platform tier (contacts bundled with funnels and courses); Kit prices by subscriber count (email-only, scaling with list size). Kit's free plan is far more generous; systeme.io's paid tiers are far cheaper.

| Tier | systeme.io | Kit (ConvertKit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free plan | $0 — 2,000 contacts, 3 funnels, 1 course, 1 automation rule, unlimited emails, no credit card | $0 — up to 10,000 subscribers, unlimited emails, forms, landing pages; 1 basic automation (no sequences) |
| Entry paid | Startup — $17/mo ($14.17/mo annual): 5,000 contacts, 10 funnels, 5 courses, 10 automation rules | Creator — $39/mo ($33/mo annual) for 1,000 subscribers: unlimited automations, sequences, Creator Network |
| Mid paid | Webinar — $47/mo ($39.17/mo annual): 10,000 contacts, evergreen webinars, 100 automation rules | Creator Pro — $79/mo ($66/mo annual) for 1,000 subscribers: advanced reporting, subscriber scoring, referral system |
| Top paid | Unlimited — $97/mo ($80.90/mo annual): unlimited everything | Pricing scales with list: Creator at 10,000 subs is ~$139/mo; at 50,000 subs ~$379/mo |

Starting prices verified September 2026 against published pricing pages and multiple 2026 pricing breakdowns. Kit's subscriber-scaled pricing changes with list size — confirm your tier on the vendor's pricing page before buying.

## The creator math at three list sizes

Scenario A: new creator, 800 subscribers, selling a first mini-course. Kit: free plan covers everything except sequences ($0). systeme.io: free plan covers 2,000 contacts plus the course and funnels ($0). Both are free — but only systeme.io hosts the course and checkout. If you're selling, systeme.io's free tier is the complete business; Kit's free tier is the complete newsletter.

Scenario B: newsletter-first creator, 3,000 subscribers, no products yet. Kit Creator: $59/month with the best automation builder in the creator space. systeme.io Startup: $17/month with unlimited emails — but the email tooling is simpler and the deliverability reputation isn't Kit's. If email revenue is the business, Kit's $42/month premium buys demonstrably better tooling; if you're building toward selling, systeme.io keeps the door open.

Scenario C: established creator, 10,000 subscribers, selling courses. Kit Creator: ~$139/month for email alone — plus a course platform ($39–$179/month elsewhere), plus a funnel builder. Realistic stack: $200+/month. systeme.io Webinar: $47/month for email, funnels, courses, and webinars combined. At this size the math isn't close — unless your email list is your #1 revenue driver, in which case Kit's automation quality can pay for itself in conversion rate.

The pattern: Kit's pricing scales with your success (which stings precisely when revenue arrives); systeme.io's pricing scales with platform tiers (which stays flat as your list grows). Newsletter-first businesses outgrow systeme.io's email depth; product businesses outgrow Kit's pricing.

## Feature comparison

systeme.io wins breadth: funnels, course hosting on all plans, evergreen webinars from $47/month, affiliate management, and checkout with no transaction fees. Kit wins email depth: visual automation builder, subscriber scoring, A/B testing, best-in-class deliverability, and the Creator Network for list growth. Kit's scaling is the catch — ~$139/month at 10,000 subscribers, ~$379/month at 50,000 — while systeme.io caps at $97.

| Feature | systeme.io | Kit (ConvertKit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email broadcasts & sequences | Yes — unlimited sending on all plans, rules-based automation | Yes — visual automation builder, sequences (paid plans) |
| Automation depth | Rules-based; 1 / 10 / 100 / unlimited rules by tier | Visual workflows, subscriber scoring (Pro), A/B testing |
| Deliverability reputation | Solid, not a differentiator | Best-in-class for creators — consistently top-rated in deliverability tests |
| Sales funnels & pages | Yes — funnels, landing pages, checkout | Basic landing pages and forms only |
| Courses & memberships | Yes — on all plans, including free | No — commerce features for digital products only |
| Webinars | Evergreen webinars (Webinar plan, $47/mo+) | No |
| Commerce / payments | Checkout via Stripe/PayPal, no platform transaction fees | Built-in commerce — paid subscriptions, digital products |
| Creator Network | No | Yes — cross-promotion with other newsletters for list growth |
| Free migration | Advertised on Unlimited plan | Yes — free list migration on paid plans |
| SMS marketing | No | No |
| Learning curve | Gentle — one dashboard for everything | Gentle — email-focused, famously easy automations |

Feature availability compiled from official documentation and 2026 comparisons. Vendors move features between tiers — confirm on the vendor's site.

## Email quality vs stack breadth

Kit's edge — and it's the whole product. Kit's visual automation builder is consistently rated the easiest serious automation tool in email marketing, its deliverability tests at the top of creator-focused tools, and features like the Creator Network (newsletter cross-promotion) and built-in paid subscriptions are genuine growth levers for publishers. The free plan — 10,000 subscribers, unlimited emails — is the most generous in email marketing. For a writer or podcaster whose business is the list, this is the professional choice.

systeme.io's edge — and it's the whole stack. Everything Kit doesn't do, systeme.io does for $17/month: funnels, checkout, course hosting, evergreen webinars, affiliate management. The email tool is simpler — rules instead of visual workflows, no subscriber scoring — but it's unlimited on every plan and perfectly adequate for launches, welcome sequences, and course drips. For a creator who sells things, the question isn't "is the email better" but "is the email $120/month better than having funnels and courses included."

## Who should pick Systeme.io, and who should pick Kit?

Pick systeme.io if you sell courses, coaching, or digital products and want funnels, email, checkout, and course hosting in one dashboard — free to $17–$47/month. Pick Kit if email is your primary channel: the best automation builder in the creator space, with a free plan covering 10,000 subscribers.

### Pick systeme.io if…

- You sell courses, coaching, or digital products

- You want funnels, email, and courses in one dashboard

- Your list is growing and Kit's pricing stings

- You need evergreen webinars ($47/mo tier)

- You want to start free with a complete business stack

### Pick Kit if…

- You're newsletter-first: writers, podcasters, publishers

- Email automation quality is your revenue lever

- You want the Creator Network for list growth

- Deliverability is a top concern

- The free plan (10,000 subs) covers your needs

## Quick answers

### Is systeme.io or Kit cheaper for a 10,000-subscriber list?

systeme.io. Its $47/month Webinar tier ($39.17 annual) covers 10,000 contacts plus funnels, courses, and checkout. Kit's Creator Pro runs $79/month ($66 annual) for 1,000 subscribers with costs rising as you grow. Kit's free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers, but advanced automation paywalls kick in — so heavy-volume publishers pay more on Kit.

### Which has better email automation — systeme.io or Kit?

Kit. Its automation builder is the best in the creator space, purpose-built for publishers where email is the primary channel. systeme.io's automation is serviceable, but its edge is breadth: email plus funnels, checkout, and course hosting in one dashboard. Publishers buy Kit for the automation; sellers buy systeme.io for the stack.

### Can I start free on both systeme.io and Kit?

Yes. systeme.io's free plan includes 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, and one automation rule; Kit's free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers with unlimited emails, forms, and landing pages. Sellers outgrow systeme.io's free tier first; publishers hit Kit's free automation limits first.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Kit still called ConvertKit?**

Kit rebranded from ConvertKit in 2024 — same company, same product, expanded scope (commerce, sponsorships, creator profiles). Older comparisons and affiliate content still say “ConvertKit,” while the pricing page now says Kit. Treat the two names as interchangeable when you're reading reviews written before the rebrand.

**Can I really use Kit free with 10,000 subscribers?**

Yes — the Newsletter plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers with unlimited emails, forms, and landing pages, no credit card required. The real limits: one basic automation and no sequences until you pay. It's the most generous free tier in email marketing.

**Which is better for selling an online course?**

systeme.io — it hosts the course, builds the sales funnel, and processes checkout in the same $17–$47/month plan. Kit handles the email marketing well but needs a separate course platform, which is where the stack cost doubles. One bill versus two integrations is the deciding factor for most course creators.

**Does systeme.io's email deliver as well as Kit's?**

Kit has the stronger deliverability reputation in 2026 tests and reviews — it's a core differentiator the company invests in. systeme.io's deliverability is reported as solid but not best-in-class. If inbox placement is your revenue lever, that matters; for launches and course drips, most users won't feel the difference.

**Can I migrate from Kit to systeme.io later (or vice versa)?**

Both support CSV contact imports, and Kit advertises free migrations on paid plans; systeme.io advertises migration assistance on its Unlimited plan. Expect to rebuild automations manually — sequences don't transfer between platforms. Budget a weekend for a simple list, longer for complex workflows.

**Why does Kit get so expensive as my list grows?**

Kit prices by subscriber count — Creator runs $39/month at 1,000 subs, ~$89 at 5,000, ~$139 at 10,000. It's the standard email-platform model, and it means your bill grows with your success. Systeme.io's flat tier pricing ($17–$97/month) is the structural alternative — the trade-off is simpler email tooling.

**systeme.io vs Kit — which is better?**

Different buyers. Pick systeme.io if you sell courses, coaching, or digital products and want funnels, email, checkout, and course hosting in one dashboard — starting free, paid tiers at $17–$97/mo. Pick Kit if email is your primary channel: the best automation builder in the creator space, with a free plan covering 10,000 subscribers.

**How much does Kit cost for 10,000 subscribers?**

Kit's Creator plan is priced per subscriber: $39/mo ($33/mo annual) for 1,000, ~$139/mo at 10,000, ~$379/mo at 50,000. Kit's free plan covers up to 10,000 subscribers, but sequences and unlimited automations need a paid plan. That pricing curve is the main argument for systeme.io's flat $97/mo Unlimited.

**Is systeme.io actually free?**

Yes, for real: the $0 plan includes 2,000 contacts, 3 funnels, 1 course, 1 automation rule, and unlimited emails with no credit card. Paid tiers: Startup $17/mo ($14.17/mo annual), Webinar $47/mo ($39.17/mo annual), and Unlimited $97/mo for unlimited everything. That makes it the lowest-risk way to start selling online today.

**Which is better for selling courses: systeme.io or Kit?**

This one isn't close. systeme.io wins for course sellers: course and membership hosting is built in on every plan, including free, alongside funnels and checkout. Kit is email-first — basic landing pages and forms only, with commerce features limited to digital products. If courses are the product, systeme.io is the tool.

**What's the real catch of systeme.io's $97/mo Unlimited plan?**

Automation depth and deliverability. systeme.io's automation is rules-based (1 / 10 / 100 / unlimited rules by tier) versus Kit's visual workflows with subscriber scoring and A/B testing — and its deliverability is solid but not the best-in-class reputation Kit holds with creators. Unlimited everything at $97/mo is real; it just trades depth for breadth.

**Can I sell digital products with systeme.io's free plan?**

Yes. systeme.io's free plan includes 2,000 contacts, 3 funnels, 1 course, unlimited emails, and checkout via Stripe/PayPal with no platform transaction fees — no credit card required. The free-plan limits that matter for sellers: 1 course, 3 funnels, and 1 automation rule. It's a genuine $0 storefront for ebooks, templates, and printables.

**Which is better for authors and book launches?**

Depends on the book's job. If the newsletter is the business, Kit: the best automation builder for publishers, best-in-class deliverability, and a free plan covering 10,000 subscribers (no sequences free). If you sell the book directly — funnels, checkout, upsells — systeme.io gives you the storefront free to $17/month with email included.

## Final verdict

Worth it for sellers: systeme.io. Email, funnels, courses, and checkout for $0–$47/month is unmatched stack value. The email tool is simpler than Kit's, but when your revenue comes from products, the funnel matters more than the workflow builder.

Worth it for publishers: Kit. If email is the business — newsletter, paid subscriptions, sponsorships — Kit's automation builder, deliverability, and Creator Network are worth the subscriber-scaled pricing. And the free plan means many creators never pay at all.

Skip systeme.io if you're a pure newsletter business with no products — you'll use 20% of the platform. Skip Kit if you sell courses or coaching — you'll pay $139+/month for email and still need a course platform on top.

### Ready to decide?

Both start free — run your actual list size through both pricing pages before committing.
